objects.description: Linked-list node describing an extended wiringPi device. Holds a pin range, device-specific fields (fd, data0-3), and function pointers implementing GPIO operations for pins in this node. The next pointer chains multiple nodes. Constructed and managed by wiringPi via wiringPiNewNode and linked through the global wiringPiNodes. Users typically do not allocate directly; they supply function pointers when creating custom devices.

Enumeration selecting the numbering scheme for pins: BCM GPIO numbers, WiringPi virtual numbers, or physical header numbers. Used when setting up wiringPi or GPIO device pin mapping.

functions.name: piGpioLayoutOops
functions.description: Internal helper to report a GPIO layout error condition. Likely logs/prints a diagnostic and may abort depending on configuration. Intended for internal use.
requirements: Parameter why should point to a valid, null-terminated string describing the issue.

functions.name: wiringPiFailure
functions.description: Internal/common error-reporting function. Formats message with variadic arguments and handles it according to fatal policy (WPI_FATAL / WPI_ALMOST). Returns an int status.
requirements: fatal should be one of WPI_FATAL or WPI_ALMOST.
message must be a valid printf-style format string when variadic arguments are supplied.

functions.name: wiringPiFindNode
functions.description: Look up an extended wiringPi device node that covers the given pin in the linked list of wiringPiNodeStruct. Returns the node pointer or NULL if not found.
requirements: pin is an integer pin index in the extended pin space; valid ranges depend on nodes previously registered via wiringPiNewNode.

functions.name: wiringPiNewNode
functions.description: Create/register a new extended device node for pins in the range [pinBase, pinBase+numPins-1] and link it into wiringPiNodes. Returns the new node or NULL on failure.
requirements: pinBase is the starting pin number for this node.
numPins is the count of pins for the node and should be positive.
Caller is expected to fill the node’s function pointers (pinMode, pullUpDnControl, digitalRead, etc.) before use.

functions.name: wiringPiVersion
functions.description: Retrieve the wiringPi library version numbers.
requirements: major must be a non-null pointer to int.
minor must be a non-null pointer to int.

functions.name: wiringPiGlobalMemoryAccess
functions.description: Report whether global memory-mapped GPIO access is available/enabled (Interface V3.3).

functions.name: wiringPiUserLevelAccess
functions.description: Report whether user-level (non-root) access to GPIO is available.

functions.name: wiringPiSetup
functions.description: Initialize wiringPi using its own pin numbering scheme. Must be called before most GPIO functions.
requirements: Call once before using pin functions like pinMode/digitalWrite/etc.
Returns 0 on success (typical); caller should check for errors before proceeding.

functions.name: wiringPiSetupSys
functions.description: Initialize wiringPi to use the sysfs (deprecated since 3.2) GPIO interface. Generally deprecated; use other setup modes.
requirements: Call before using GPIO functions if using sysfs mode.
Deprecated; new code should avoid this mode.

functions.name: wiringPiSetupGpio
functions.description: Initialize wiringPi with Broadcom (BCM) GPIO numbering.
requirements: Call before using GPIO functions when addressing pins by BCM numbers.
Check return value for success before proceeding.

functions.name: wiringPiSetupPhys
functions.description: Initialize wiringPi with physical header pin numbering.
requirements: Call before using GPIO functions when addressing by physical header pin numbers.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: wiringPiSetupPinType
functions.description: Initialize wiringPi to use the specified pin numbering type (BCM/WPI/PHYS). Interface V3.3.
requirements: pinType must be one of WPI_PIN_BCM, WPI_PIN_WPI, or WPI_PIN_PHYS.
Must be called before other GPIO operations.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: wiringPiSetupGpioDevice
functions.description: Initialize wiringPi to use the Linux gpiochip character device with the specified numbering type. Interface V3.3.
requirements: pinType must be one of WPI_PIN_BCM, WPI_PIN_WPI, or WPI_PIN_PHYS.
Must be called before using GPIO functions when targeting the gpio device backend.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: wiringPiGpioDeviceGetFd
functions.description: Return the file descriptor associated with the gpio device backend (Interface V3.3).
requirements: Must have been initialized via wiringPiSetupGpioDevice or compatible setup before calling.

functions.name: pinModeAlt
functions.description: Set a pin to an alternate function (ALT modes) instead of simple input/output.
requirements: pin identifies the pin according to the active numbering scheme.
mode must be a valid alternate selection; typically use WPIPinAlt or getAlt/getPinModeAlt conventions.

functions.name: getPinModeAlt
functions.description: Return the current alternate function setting for a pin as WPIPinAlt (Interface V3.5).
requirements: pin identifies the pin according to the active numbering scheme.

functions.name: pinMode
functions.description: Configure a pin’s basic mode (INPUT, OUTPUT, PWM_OUTPUT, SOFT_PWM_OUTPUT, etc.).
requirements: Call a wiringPi setup function first.
pin is addressed per the current numbering mode.
mode must be one of the defined mode constants (INPUT, OUTPUT, PWM_OUTPUT, GPIO_CLOCK, SOFT_PWM_OUTPUT, SOFT_TONE_OUTPUT, PWM_TONE_OUTPUT, PM_OFF, etc.).

functions.name: pullUpDnControl
functions.description: Enable or disable the internal pull-up or pull-down resistor on a pin.
requirements: Call a wiringPi setup function first.
pin is addressed per the current numbering mode.
pud must be PUD_OFF, PUD_DOWN, or PUD_UP.

functions.name: digitalRead
functions.description: Read the digital logic level from a pin. Returns LOW or HIGH.
requirements: Call a wiringPi setup function first.
pin is addressed per the current numbering mode.
The pin should be configured as INPUT (or a readable mode).

functions.name: digitalWrite
functions.description: Set a pin to a digital logic level.
requirements: Call a wiringPi setup function first.
pin is addressed per the current numbering mode.
value must be LOW or HIGH.
The pin should be configured as OUTPUT (or a writable mode).

functions.name: pwmWrite
functions.description: Write a PWM value to a pin configured for hardware or software PWM.
requirements: Call a wiringPi setup function first.
pin is addressed per the current numbering mode and must support/configured for PWM.
Valid value range depends on the configured PWM range via pwmSetRange (exact numeric range not specified here).

functions.name: analogRead
functions.description: Read an analog value from a pin via an attached/extended device node (not native to Raspberry Pi GPIO).
requirements: The specified pin must be provided by a wiringPiNodeStruct that implements analogRead.
Call the appropriate setup and ensure the node’s analogRead function pointer is set.

functions.name: analogWrite
functions.description: Write an analog value (typically via PWM or DAC on an extended device) to a pin.
requirements: The specified pin must belong to a device/node that implements analogWrite.
value range depends on the device; not specified here.
Ensure device node is registered and initialized.

functions.name: wiringPiSetupPiFace

requirements: Deprecated; new code should avoid using this.
Call before PiFace-specific GPIO operations if you still use it.

functions.name: wiringPiSetupPiFaceForGpioProg
functions.description: Initialize PiFace for the gpio utility program. Not for general use.
requirements: Do not use in general applications; for gpio program only.

functions.name: piGpioLayout
functions.description: Return the GPIO layout identifier for the current Raspberry Pi model.

functions.name: piBoardRev

requirements: Prefer piGpioLayout for new code.

functions.description: Return a code identifying the RP1 model (Interface V3.14), applicable to newer Raspberry Pi versions.

functions.name: wpiPinToGpio
functions.description: Convert a wiringPi pin number to a BCM GPIO number.

wpiPin must be within supported range for the active model/layout.

functions.name: physPinToGpio
functions.description: Convert a physical header pin number to a BCM GPIO number.
requirements: Commented restriction: please don't use outside 0–63 and on RP1.
physPin must be a valid physical pin for the board.

functions.name: setPadDrive
functions.description: Set the pad drive strength for a group of GPIO pads.
requirements: group identifies a pad group; valid values depend on SoC (not specified here).
value is the drive strength setting; valid range not specified here.
Requires proper setup and permissions to change pad controls.

functions.name: setPadDrivePin
functions.description: Set the pad drive strength for a specific pin (Interface V3.0).
requirements: pin is addressed per the current numbering mode.
value is the drive strength; numeric range not specified.
Requires appropriate privileges to alter pad settings.

functions.name: getAlt
functions.description: Return the raw alternate function number for a pin.
requirements: pin is addressed per the current numbering mode.

functions.name: pwmToneWrite
functions.description: Generate a tone by configuring PWM on the specified pin to a given frequency.
requirements: pin must support/configured for PWM tone output (e.g., PWM_TONE_OUTPUT).
freq is in Hz; valid ranges depend on hardware/clock settings (not specified).
Call setup first.

functions.name: pwmSetMode
functions.description: Set PWM mode to mark-space (PWM_MODE_MS) or balanced (PWM_MODE_BAL).
requirements: mode must be PWM_MODE_MS or PWM_MODE_BAL.
Effective only on hardware PWM-capable channels.

functions.name: pwmSetRange
functions.description: Set the PWM range (top value) used by pwmWrite for hardware PWM.
requirements: range defines the maximum PWM count; specific acceptable values depend on hardware; not specified.
Call after setup and before pwmWrite for intended scaling.

functions.name: pwmSetClock
functions.description: Set the PWM clock divisor controlling the base PWM frequency.
requirements: divisor sets clock division; valid range not specified here.
Changing clock affects PWM frequency across channels.

functions.name: gpioClockSet
functions.description: Configure a GPIO clock output on a pin at the specified frequency.
requirements: pin must support GPIO clock mode (GPIO_CLOCK).
freq is the target frequency in Hz; valid range depends on hardware; not specified.
Call setup first.

functions.name: digitalReadByte
functions.description: Read the logic levels of the first 8 GPIOs as a bit mask.
requirements: Interpretation depends on current numbering/backend; ensure setup has been called.

functions.name: digitalReadByte2
functions.description: Read the logic levels of the second bank of 8 GPIOs as a bit mask.
requirements: Interpretation depends on current numbering/backend; ensure setup has been called.

functions.name: digitalWriteByte
functions.description: Write logic levels to the first 8 GPIOs using the lower 8 bits of value.
requirements: Ensure pins are configured as outputs as needed.
Only the low byte of value is used; other bits are ignored.

functions.name: digitalWriteByte2
functions.description: Write logic levels to the second bank of 8 GPIOs using the lower 8 bits of value.
requirements: Ensure those pins are configured as outputs as needed.
Only the low byte of value is used.

functions.name: wiringPiISR

functions.description: Attach an interrupt service routine to a pin for the specified edge mode. The callback is invoked on interrupts.

pin is addressed per the active numbering mode.
mode must be one of INT_EDGE_SETUP, INT_EDGE_FALLING, INT_EDGE_RISING, or INT_EDGE_BOTH.

functions.description: Wait for an interrupt on a pin with edge selection, timeout, and debounce. Returns a WPIWfiStatus describing the result (V3.16).
requirements: pin is addressed per the active numbering mode.
edgeMode must be INT_EDGE_FALLING, INT_EDGE_RISING, INT_EDGE_BOTH, or INT_EDGE_SETUP as appropriate.
ms is the timeout in milliseconds; if it times out, statusOK will be 0.
debounce_period_us is the debounce period in microseconds.

functions.name: wiringPiISR2
functions.signature: int  wiringPiISR2       (int pin, int edgeMode, void (*function)(struct WPIWfiStatus wfiStatus, void* userdata), unsigned long debounce_period_us, void* userdata);
functions.description: Attach an interrupt handler with extended status and user data, including debounce control (V3.16).
requirements: Call a wiringPi setup function first.
pin is addressed per the active numbering mode.
edgeMode must be an INT_EDGE_* constant.
function must be a valid, non-null callback pointer.
debounce_period_us specifies debounce in microseconds; non-negative.
userdata may be NULL or any pointer the callback expects.

functions.name: wiringPiISRStop
functions.description: Detach/stop the interrupt handler associated with the given pin (V3.2).
requirements: pin is addressed per the active numbering mode.
Should be called to clean up previously registered ISR on that pin.

functions.name: waitForInterruptClose
functions.description: Legacy alias for stopping interrupt wait/handling on a pin; use wiringPiISRStop instead (V3.2).
requirements: pin is addressed per the active numbering mode.
Prefer wiringPiISRStop for new code.

functions.name: piThreadCreate
functions.description: Create a new thread that starts at fn(void*). Returns a status code or thread id depending on implementation.
requirements: fn must be a valid function pointer of type void* (*)(void*).
The function must be callable and handle its own argument (implementation-dependent).

functions.name: piLock
functions.description: Acquire a simple library-managed lock identified by key to synchronize threads.
requirements: key identifies the lock; valid key ranges are not specified here.

functions.name: piUnlock
functions.description: Release a lock previously acquired with piLock for the given key.
requirements: key must match a previously locked key in the calling context.

functions.name: piHiPri

requirements: pri is the desired priority; acceptable range/platform requirements are not specified.
Caller should check return value to ensure the priority change succeeded.

requirements: ms is the number of milliseconds to delay; values are unsigned (non-negative).

functions.name: delayMicroseconds

requirements: us is the number of microseconds to delay; values are unsigned (non-negative).

functions.name: wiringPiI2CRead
functions.description: Reads a single byte from the current address/command on the I2C device referenced by fd. Typical usage is after setting the device’s internal address pointer (via a prior register write) or for devices that stream data. Returns the read byte on success or a negative value on error (pattern inferred from wiringPi conventions).
requirements: fd must be a valid, open I2C device file descriptor obtained from wiringPiI2CSetup or wiringPiI2CSetupInterface.
Caller must check the return value; a negative value indicates an error (inferred from wiringPi patterns).
The device must support a single-byte read at its current internal address/pointer (device-specific; exact behavior unknown).

functions.name: wiringPiI2CReadReg8
functions.description: Reads an 8-bit value from register reg on the I2C device referenced by fd. Returns the 8-bit value (0–255) on success or a negative value on error (pattern inferred).
requirements: fd must be a valid, open I2C device file descriptor from wiringPiI2CSetup or wiringPiI2CSetupInterface.
reg must be a valid register address for the target device; exact valid range is device-specific and not defined here (likely 8-bit, but unknown).
Caller must check the return value; a negative value indicates an error (inferred).

functions.name: wiringPiI2CReadReg16
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit value from register reg on the I2C device referenced by fd. Returns the 16-bit value (0–65535) on success or a negative value on error (pattern inferred). Endianness/order is library/device-specific and not stated here.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open I2C device file descriptor from wiringPiI2CSetup or wiringPiI2CSetupInterface.
reg must be a valid register address for the target device; valid range is device-specific and not defined here.
Caller must check the return value; a negative value indicates an error (inferred).
Be aware of potential byte-order/endian expectations of the target device; exact ordering is not specified here.

functions.name: wiringPiI2CReadBlockData
functions.signature: int wiringPiI2CReadBlockData(int fd, int reg, uint8_t *values, uint8_t size);
functions.description: Reads a block of size bytes starting at register reg from the I2C device referenced by fd into values. Returns a non-negative result on success (semantics not explicitly documented; typically number of bytes read) or a negative value on error (pattern inferred).
requirements: fd must be a valid, open I2C device file descriptor from wiringPiI2CSetup or wiringPiI2CSetupInterface.
values must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer with capacity of at least size bytes.
size must fit in uint8_t (0–255 by type); the supported maximum may be limited by the device/controller but is not specified here.
reg must be a valid starting register address for the device; addressability and block behavior are device-specific.
Caller must check the return value; a negative value indicates an error (inferred).

functions.name: wiringPiI2CRawRead
functions.signature: int wiringPiI2CRawRead(int fd, uint8_t *values, uint8_t size);
functions.description: Performs a raw I2C read of size bytes from the device referenced by fd into values, without specifying a register. Returns a non-negative result on success (typically number of bytes read) or a negative value on error (pattern inferred).
requirements: fd must be a valid, open I2C device file descriptor from wiringPiI2CSetup or wiringPiI2CSetupInterface.
values must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer with capacity of at least size bytes.
size must fit in uint8_t (0–255 by type); the effective maximum depends on the device/controller and is not specified here.
The target device must support raw sequential reads as used by this call; exact semantics are device-specific.
Caller must check the return value; a negative value indicates an error (inferred).

The device must support a single-byte write operation without a register (device-specific).
Caller must check the return value; a negative value indicates an error (inferred).

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: POSIX filesystem path strings used by wiringPiI2CSetupInterface and serialOpen.
# We generate a single bytes buffer that the fuzzer will split/consume via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Strategy:
# - Include highly-likely valid device paths (/dev/i2c-1, /dev/i2c-0, /dev/tty*, /dev/pts/*, /dev/null).
# - Mix in temporary file paths under /tmp and /dev/shm that look realistic.
# - Sometimes emit relative paths and edge cases (dotfiles, long names, nested dirs) but remain syntactically valid.
# - Ensure NUL termination expectation is met by returning ASCII bytes without embedded NUL; the harness will NUL-terminate.
# - Keep under 4096 bytes.

COMMON_I2C = [
    "/dev/i2c-1",
    "/dev/i2c-0",
    "/dev/i2c-10",
]

COMMON_TTY = [
    "/dev/tty",
    "/dev/ttyS0",
    "/dev/ttyS1",
    "/dev/ttyUSB0",
    "/dev/ttyUSB1",
    "/dev/ttyAMA0",
    "/dev/ttyACM0",
    "/dev/pts/0",
]

COMMON_MISC = [
    "/dev/null",
    "/dev/zero",
    "/dev/random",
    "/dev/urandom",
]

TMP_BASES = ["/tmp", "/dev/shm", "/run/user/1000", ".", "./.cache"]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-"


def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_dirpath(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(TMP_BASES)
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    parts: List[str] = [base]
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_name(rng))
    return "/".join(parts).replace("//", "/")


def _rand_device_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create device-like names under /dev to exercise different code paths
    choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        # i2c-X with 0..15
        return f"/dev/i2c-{rng.randint(0,15)}"
    if choice == 1:
        # ttyS, ttyUSB, ttyACM
        kind = rng.choice(["ttyS", "ttyUSB", "ttyACM", "ttyAMA"])
        return f"/dev/{kind}{rng.randint(0,5)}"
    if choice == 2:
        # pts
        return f"/dev/pts/{rng.randint(0,4)}"
    if choice == 3:
        # spi and i2c alternates
        return f"/dev/spidev{rng.randint(0,1)}.{rng.randint(0,1)}"
    # generic
    return f"/dev/{_rand_name(rng)}"


def _weighted_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    paths: List[str] = []
    # Heavily weight common valid special files
    for _ in range(3):
        paths.append(rng.choice(COMMON_I2C))
    for _ in range(3):
        paths.append(rng.choice(COMMON_TTY))
    for _ in range(2):
        paths.append(rng.choice(COMMON_MISC))

    # Add several device-like variants
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)):
        paths.append(_rand_device_like(rng))

    # Add temp files (some with nested directories)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)):
        d = _rand_dirpath(rng)
        fname = _rand_name(rng, 4, 16)
        paths.append(f"{d}/{fname}")

    # Relative and edge-but-valid
    paths.extend([
        "./device", "../dev/mock", ".hidden", "./.dotdir/file", "./i2c-virt",
    ])

    # Ensure uniqueness while preserving some duplicates for weighting
    # Keep order deterministic per seed by stable filtering
    seen = set()
    unique_paths: List[str] = []
    for p in paths:
        if p not in seen or rng.random() < 0.2:  # allow occasional duplicates
            unique_paths.append(p)
            seen.add(p)
    return unique_paths


def _serialize_paths(paths: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join with newlines; FUZZ_PARAM_STR typically consumes slices from a shared buffer.
    # Newline separators help the harness split distinct strings.
    blob = "\n".join(paths)
    # Limit size to 4096 bytes
    b = blob.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
        # avoid cutting multi-byte, but we used ASCII-safe set mostly; still safe.
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide a theme to bias towards I2C or Serial to match the two stubs
    theme = rng.choice(["i2c-heavy", "serial-heavy", "mixed"])    
    paths = _weighted_paths(rng)

    if theme == "i2c-heavy":
        # Prepend multiple strong candidates for I2C
        bias = [
            "/dev/i2c-1", "/dev/i2c-0", "/dev/i2c-10",
            _rand_device_like(rng), _rand_device_like(rng)
        ]
        paths = bias + paths
    elif theme == "serial-heavy":
        bias = [
            "/dev/ttyS0", "/dev/ttyUSB0", "/dev/ttyACM0", "/dev/tty", "/dev/pts/0",
            _rand_device_like(rng), _rand_device_like(rng)
        ]
        paths = bias + paths
    else:
        # Mixed: start with /dev/null to allow serialOpen to succeed but fail termios in interesting ways
        paths = ["/dev/null", "/dev/tty", "/dev/i2c-1"] + paths

    # Add a few crafted long but valid paths
    long_dir = "/tmp/" + "/".join(_rand_name(rng, 8, 12) for _ in range(5))
    paths.append(f"{long_dir}/{_rand_name(rng, 20, 30)}")

    # Ensure final buffer size limit
    return _serialize_paths(paths)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target: wiringPiI2CSetupInterface stub
# The stub consumes:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): used as the device path when not choosing the default
# - FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) twice: one bit for pick_default, one value for devId selection
# We must return a bytes buffer that the fuzz harness will slice to feed those params in order.
# Assumptions about the harness (common pattern):
#   - FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) pulls 4 bytes (LE) from the buffer, advancing.
#   - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() pulls a length-prefixed or NUL-terminated string. Most harnesses using std::string
#     from a buffer do length-prefixed. To stay broadly compatible, we place a short length and then that
#     many bytes of content; if the harness instead scans to NUL, we include a NUL early.
# Strategy:
#   - Provide both possibilities: begin with an unsigned int for pick_default, then a string blob that
#     contains a valid device path and a NUL early, then another unsigned int for devId randomness.
#   - We randomize whether pick_default selects the realistic default (/dev/i2c-1) or the fuzzed path.
#   - For the fuzzed path, we generate plausible Linux I2C device nodes and a few variants, including
#     common ones like /dev/i2c-0, /dev/i2c-1, /dev/i2c-10, /dev/i2c-7, and a short custom path.
#   - Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes.

_VALID_I2C_PATHS = [
    b"/dev/i2c-1",
    b"/dev/i2c-0",
    b"/dev/i2c-10",
    b"/dev/i2c-7",
    b"/dev/i2c-5",
    b"/dev/i2c-3",
]

def _pack_u32_le(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _make_str_blob(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Provide both a length prefix and an early NUL to satisfy different FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers.
    # Layout: [u32 length][bytes][NUL]
    # The stub caps to 255 chars; we keep <= 255.
    data = s[:255]
    return _pack_u32_le(len(data)) + data + b"\x00"

def _random_i2c_path(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        return rng.choice(_VALID_I2C_PATHS)
    elif choice == 1:
        # /dev/i2c-N where N in 0..15
        n = rng.randint(0, 15)
        return f"/dev/i2c-{n}".encode()
    elif choice == 2:
        # Symlink-like plausible alias path (still a file path string)
        n = rng.randint(0, 1)
        return (b"/dev/serial/by-path/platform-i2c-" + str(n).encode())
    elif choice == 3:
        # Slightly longer but still under cap
        bus = rng.randint(0, 3)
        cs = rng.randint(0, 1)
        return f"/dev/i2c-{bus}".encode()
    else:
        # Fallback to valid list
        return rng.choice(_VALID_I2C_PATHS)

def _random_dev_id(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # 7-bit I2C usable range 0x03..0x77
    return rng.randint(0x03, 0x77)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide whether to pick default device path or fuzzed path
    pick_default = rng.choice([0, 1])

    # First FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int): controls pick_default bit in stub (only LSB used)
    first_u32 = (1 if pick_default else 0)

    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): path
    if pick_default:
        path = b"/dev/i2c-1"
    else:
        path = _random_i2c_path(rng)

    # Second FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int): influences devId mapping
    dev_id = _random_dev_id(rng)

    # Assemble buffer: [u32 pick_default][str blob][u32 devId]
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += _pack_u32_le(first_u32)
    buf += _make_str_blob(path)
    buf += _pack_u32_le(dev_id)

    # Ensure size limit
    return bytes(buf[:4096])

    out.extend(rng.sample(COMMON_BAUDS, k=min(len(COMMON_BAUDS), max(3, count // 2))))
    # Add some random valid positive ints in 1..1_000_000 per stub default branch
    for _ in range(max(2, count - len(out))):
        out.append(rng.randint(1, 1_000_000))
    return out


def _build_sequence(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    seq: List[int] = []

    # First integer biases device selection
    seq.append(rng.choice(DEVICE_PICKERS))

    # Second integer biases baud mode selection (mod 6)
    seq.append(rng.choice(MODE_PICKERS))

    # Third integer used when mode falls to default path to supply a large random
    # positive; we still provide it even if not used by the run, as the stub may
    # pull additional integers from the same buffer.
    seq.append(rng.randint(1, 1_000_000))

    # Mix in an assortment of interesting edges
    seq.extend(rng.sample(INTERESTING_INTS, k=min(8, len(INTERESTING_INTS))))

    # Append several plausible baud rates
    seq.extend(_sample_bauds(rng, count=8))

    # Add more device/mode pickers to allow multiple invocations within the same
    # input to exercise different branches.
    for _ in range(4):
        seq.append(rng.choice(DEVICE_PICKERS))
        seq.append(rng.choice(MODE_PICKERS))
        seq.append(rng.randint(1, 1_000_000))

    return seq


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    seq = _build_sequence(rng)

    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes; trim if necessary
    data = _encode_numbers(seq)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # Trim by reducing the number of trailing entries
        while len(data) > 4096 and seq:
            seq.pop()
            data = _encode_numbers(seq)
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for an "arbitrary string" suitable for multiple stubs expecting C strings.
# Goals:
# - Always NUL-terminated when consumed via c_str() by the stubs.
# - Include interesting patterns to exercise formatting (printf), device names, and parser-like inputs.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic w.r.t. the provided seed while remaining varied.

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_PRINTABLE = string.printable
_HEX = '0123456789abcdef'


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Allow a mix of whitespace, punctuation and alphanumerics
    choices = _PRINTABLE
    return ''.join(r.choice(choices) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_bytes_as_text(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include some NUL-unsafe bytes replaced with escape-like sequences to keep as text
    return ''.join(chr(r.randint(1, 255)) if r.random() < 0.85 else '\\x%02x' % r.randint(0, 255) for _ in range(n))


def _fmt_integer_patterns(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    a = r.randint(-2**31, 2**31-1)
    b = r.getrandbits(32)
    c = r.getrandbits(32)
    d = r.randint(-2**31, 2**31-1)
    return [
        "hello world",
        f"{a} {b} {b:x}",
        f"val={d} str=%s",  # includes %s to test literal percent handling in some paths
        f"chars {chr(32 + (b % 95))} {chr(32 + (c % 95))}",
        f"mix {a} example {b} 0x{b:X}",
    ]


def _device_like_paths(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Common serial device candidates to exercise serialOpen/usage-like contexts
    bases = ["/dev/ttyS", "/dev/ttyAMA", "/dev/ttyUSB", "/dev/ttyACM"]
    entries = []
    for b in bases:
        entries.append(f"{b}{r.randint(0, 9)}")
    return entries


def _legacy_revision_lines(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    vals = [r.getrandbits(16), r.getrandbits(24), r.getrandbits(32)]
    lines = []
    for v in vals:
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"Revision\t: {v:x}")
        else:
            lines.append(f"Revision\t: {v % 100000}")
    return lines


def _bounded_join(parts: List[str], max_len: int, sep: str = "\n") -> str:
    out = []
    total = 0
    for p in parts:
        p2 = p
        if total + len(p2) + (len(sep) if out else 0) > max_len:
            # Truncate last piece to fit
            remaining = max_len - total - (len(sep) if out else 0)
            if remaining <= 0:
                break
            p2 = p2[:remaining]
        if out:
            out.append(sep)
            total += len(sep)
        out.append(p2)
        total += len(p2)
        if total >= max_len:
            break
    return ''.join(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Compose a bag of interesting strings
    parts: List[str] = []

    # 1) Short and long ASCII segments
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 32))
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 5, 64))

    # 2) Format-string-like but safe payloads and literals
    parts.extend(_fmt_integer_patterns(r))

    # 3) Device path candidates for serial and I2C/SPI hints
    parts.extend(_device_like_paths(r))

    # 4) Legacy revision lines for GetPiRevisionLegacy
    parts.extend(_legacy_revision_lines(r))

    # 5) Mixed hex-like tokens and random bytes-as-text
    hexblob = ''.join(r.choice(_HEX) for _ in range(r.randint(8, 64)))
    parts.append(hexblob)
    parts.append(_rand_bytes_as_text(r, 8, 96))

    # 6) Human-readable words and punctuation, including percent signs
    words = [
        "%d", "%u", "%x", "%ld", "%s", "%%",  # include literal percent
        "GPIO", "BCM", "ALT0", "PWM", "I2C", "SPI",
        "lcd", "scroll", "phat", "wiringPi", "serial",
    ]
    # Randomly shuffle and take a slice
    r.shuffle(words)
    parts.append(' '.join(words[:r.randint(5, len(words))]))

    # 7) Potentially long user string, trimmed later
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 32, 512))

    # Decide an overall target length within bounds (< 4096). Leave room for terminator when consumed.
    target_len = r.randint(64, min(2048, _MAX_TOTAL))
    s = _bounded_join(parts, target_len, sep='\n')

    # Ensure non-empty; add a newline if empty
    if not s:
        s = "\n"

    # Return as bytes; C++ stubs use std::string and c_str() for NUL termination
    data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(data) > _MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:_MAX_TOTAL]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target format: a single C string line buffer that will be copied into the fuzzer's buf, which
# ensures NUL-termination within linelength. Our goal is to provide interesting, yet valid lines
# that resemble legacy Pi revision entries and variants the parser might accept.
#
# Examples to cover:
# - Exact key with tab and colon: "Revision\t: 0002"
# - Hex without 0x: "Revision\t: a02082"
# - Upper/lower hex, variable length, with/without leading zeros
# - Extra whitespace variations
# - Key case variants: "revision", "REVISION"
# - Key/value embedded in longer strings
# - Multiple tokens on one line (parser might scan)
# - Decimal numbers
# - With trailing comments or tokens
# - Alternative separators: spaces, '='
# - Kernel cmdline-like pairs (still containing Revision token)

_HEXCHARS = "0123456789abcdef"
_HEXCHARS_UP = "0123456789ABCDEF"


def _rand_hex(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 8, upper: bool = False) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    chars = _HEXCHARS_UP if upper else _HEXCHARS
    return "".join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))


essential_keys: List[str] = [
    "Revision\t:",
    "Revision:",
    "Revision\t :",
    "Revision :",
    "revision:",
    "REVISION:",
    "Hardware\t:",  # sometimes present in cpuinfo; include to create realistic context
]


def _gen_core_line(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    key = rng.choice(essential_keys)

    # Decide value form
    form = rng.choice([
        "dec_short", "hex_short", "hex_long", "hex_upper", "hex_mixed", "dec_long",
        "prefixed_0x", "prefixed_0X", "leading_zeros", "pi4_style"
    ])

    if form == "dec_short":
        val = str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
    elif form == "dec_long":
        val = str(rng.randint(0, 10**9))
    elif form == "hex_short":
        val = _rand_hex(rng, 1, 4, upper=False)
    elif form == "hex_long":
        val = _rand_hex(rng, 5, 8, upper=False)
    elif form == "hex_upper":
        val = _rand_hex(rng, 4, 8, upper=True)
    elif form == "hex_mixed":
        # mix upper/lower
        n = rng.randint(4, 8)
        val = "".join(rng.choice((_HEXCHARS + _HEXCHARS_UP)) for _ in range(n))
    elif form == "prefixed_0x":
        val = "0x" + _rand_hex(rng, 1, 8, upper=False)
    elif form == "prefixed_0X":
        val = "0X" + _rand_hex(rng, 1, 8, upper=True)
    elif form == "leading_zeros":
        n = rng.randint(4, 8)
        core = _rand_hex(rng, 1, n, upper=False)
        val = core.rjust(n, '0')
    else:  # pi4_style placeholder: plausible long hex
        val = _rand_hex(rng, 6, 10, upper=False)

    # Random whitespace between key and value
    ws = "".join(rng.choice([" ", "\t"]) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)))
    line = f"{key}{ws}{val}"

    # Optionally append trailing comment or tokens
    tail_type = rng.choice(["none", "comment", "tokens", "spaces"]) 
    if tail_type == "comment":
        comment = rng.choice([" # rev", " ; note", " // legacy", " /*c*/"]) 
        line += comment
    elif tail_type == "tokens":
        # Append additional cpuinfo-like fields to keep realistic
        extras = []
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            extras.append(f"Hardware\t: BCM{rng.choice([2708,2709,2835,2836,2837,2711])}")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            extras.append(f"Serial\t\t: {''.join(rng.choice(string.hexdigits) for _ in range(16))}")
        sep = " | " if rng.random() < 0.5 else "  "
        line += sep + sep.join(extras)
    elif tail_type == "spaces":
        line += " " * rng.randint(1, 8)

    return line


def _embed_in_context(rng: random.Random, core: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes return just the core line; sometimes embed in a larger context where
    # the first linelength will still NUL early, but content may be copied.
    style = rng.choice(["core_only", "cpuinfo_like", "kv_pair", "cmdline_like"]) 
    if style == "core_only":
        return core
    if style == "cpuinfo_like":
        lines = []
        # some preceding lines
        prefix_count = rng.randint(0, 3)
        for _ in range(prefix_count):
            lines.append(rng.choice([
                f"Hardware\t: BCM{rng.choice([2708,2709,2835,2836,2837,2711])}",
                f"Revision\t: {_rand_hex(rng, 4, 6)}",  # decoy
                f"Model\t\t: Raspberry Pi {rng.choice(['Model B','Model B+','2 Model B','3 Model B','4 Model B'])}",
            ]))
        lines.append(core)
        # trailing lines
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
            lines.append(rng.choice([
                f"Serial\t\t: {''.join(rng.choice(string.hexdigits) for _ in range(16))}",
                f"SoC\t\t: BCM{rng.choice([2835,2836,2837,2711])}",
            ]))
        # Return only the specific line the stub will copy; since fuzzer copies only seed bytes,
        # we choose to return just the core line to keep it valid as a single line input.
        return core
    if style == "kv_pair":
        # Place key=value pairs then the core
        kvs = [
            f"model=RaspberryPi{rng.randint(1,5)}",
            f"soc=BCM{rng.choice([2835,2836,2837,2711])}",
        ]
        return (" ".join(kvs)) + " " + core
    # cmdline-like
    parts = [
        f"console=ttyAMA0,115200", f"root=/dev/mmcblk0p2", f"fsck.repair=yes",
        f"cma={rng.choice([64,128,256])}M",
    ]
    return " ".join(parts + [core])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a core valid revision-like line
    core = _gen_core_line(rng)

    # Optionally embed in a context to vary prefixes/suffixes
    line = _embed_in_context(rng, core)

    # Ensure ASCII and limit size; keep under 512 to match stub expectations comfortably.
    # Also avoid NULs because the stub will handle termination; provide a clean C-string.
    line = ''.join(ch for ch in line if ch != '\\x00')

    # Occasionally provide newline termination; otherwise raw line
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        line = line.rstrip("\n\r") + "\n"

    # Truncate conservatively to avoid exceeding the fuzzer's buf copy region
    if len(line) > 400:
        line = line[:400]

    return line.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")
